title: Social Influences in Sequential Decision Making

participants.population: Students from different departments at the University of Basel

study_1: Explain the two equally likely urns and their white/black ball compositions.
Explain that up to four people draw privately with replacement and publicly announce only their urn prediction.
Randomize all 24 scenarios independently for each participant.
For each scenario, show the previous public urn predictions and the participant's private ball color.
Collect an Urn A or Urn B prediction and a 50-100 confidence judgment.
study_2: Ask the participant to take the role of an assistant physician.
Explain the equal disease priors, symptom likelihoods, and equal two-in-three independent accuracy of assistant physicians and the medical director.
Randomize all 40 scenarios independently for each participant.
For each scenario, show the patient's private symptom and the ordered diagnoses in the patient record.
Collect an appendicitis or sigmoid diverticulitis diagnosis and a 50-100 confidence judgment.

runtime.group_semantics: participants are independent and may run in parallel; each participant receives one complete randomized sub-study
runtime.participant_count_constraint: must be even so both sub-studies receive the same number of participants
